root_cause: CWE-787: The vulnerability comes from the fact that the specification does not define the maximum number of repetitions, and there is no boundary condition checking in the parsing code. But the same time the FDD_rr_put_pncd_qmsg does define an arbitrary (as in implementation specific) limit by allocating a 128 bytes long array to store the pointers of the collected Container Data messages. The size of a pointer on either modem architecture used by Mediatek basebands (interAptive and I7200-based) is always 4 bytes, so as a result there is only 32 allocated slots. Unfortunately here the boundary check is also missing, thus with more than 32 entries it is possibile to write past the allocated chunk (qmsg->ptr_to_msg_ptr_array).

root_cause: CWE-787: The structure of “Operator-defined access category definitions” is defined in Section 9.11.3.38 of 3GPP TS 24.501. It consists of a header followed by definitions. According to the spec “The value part of the Operator-defined access category definitions information element consists of zero or no more than 32 operator-defined access category definition fields”. Shannon baseband appears to allocate space for 33 definition fields when initializing the decoder. The problem is that there is no check in the decoding function that there are less than 33 definition fields. The decoding function can instead write up to 255 (due to using an 8-bit counter) definition fields, which will cause a heap buffer overflow.
